$comment: Vendored facts-only snapshot of the peek.software teardown catalog (id, pillar, severity, points, fixSummary, languages). Regenerated by peek-software on deploy — see docs/deep-scan-engine.md §5.2. `languages` is the TD's coverage matrix (a variant may not be shipped yet); the actual executable rules live in rules/peek/<TD-id>/.

teardowns.fixSummary: Require auth, rate-limit per user, cap max_tokens, truncate input, use the cheapest model that fits the job, and set a provider-level spend alert.
Scope every query to the authenticated tenant via a compound (id + organizationId) key — and return 404 for cross-tenant lookups so the resource's existence isn't leaked.

Move the secret to the server: create the PaymentIntent in a route handler using a server-only environment variable, and have the client call that endpoint — never ship the SDK or the key to the browser.
Register on wp_ajax_ (logged-in only), verify a nonce with check_ajax_referer(), authorize with current_user_can(), and take the identity from the session — never from the request body.
Pass the raw value as a %s placeholder argument — the escaping happens inside prepare(), not in the string. Never concatenate input before preparing.
Use execFile()/spawn() with an argument array — no shell, no metacharacter interpretation — and validate the filename against an allowlist before it reaches the command.
Define the provider's contract with a runtime schema (Zod) instead of any/@ts-ignore — a shape change then fails loudly at the boundary, not silently downstream.
Catch the specific, retryable exception type — log it — and raise loudly when retries are exhausted. Never bare except, never pass.
